title: Assessment Allowance in a Summit Reserve's Property Tax Projection
content:
The assessment allowance is the percentage by which a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve under Set-Aside Accounts expects next tax year's property tax to exceed this year's. It is set from the reserve's own property tax bills in two situations.

**Terms used.** The tax year's bills are the property tax bills on file for the reserve received no later than the review date and fewer than 12 whole calendar months before it. The previous tax year's paid bills are the paid property tax bills received within the 24 months before the review less those received within the 12 months — the paid bills received at least 12 but fewer than 24 whole calendar months before the review. The most recently received unpaid property tax bill is the bill with status received and the latest received date.

| Situation in the bill file | Assessment allowance |
|---|---|
| At least one of the tax year's bills is withdrawn, at least one is received and unpaid, and the most recently received unpaid property tax bill is lower than the average billed amount of the tax year's withdrawn bills | The restoration allowance, 6.0 percent — a value lowered by a correction can be restored by the assessor the next year |
| None of the tax year's bills is withdrawn, the previous tax year's paid bills are more than zero, and the tax year's paid and received bills sum to less than the previous tax year's paid bills | Zero — a value already falling carries no increase |
| Any other file | Not set by this rule |

The average billed amount of the withdrawn bills is their total divided by their number.

**Hypothetical files.**
- Withdrawn bills 1,600.00 and 1,500.00 (average 1,550.00); a received corrected bill of 1,400.00: 1,400.00 is lower than 1,550.00, so the allowance is 6.0 percent. A corrected bill of 1,550.00 is not lower, so this rule does not set it.
- No withdrawn bill; this year paid and received 2,950.00; previous year paid 3,000.00: the allowance is zero. At exactly 3,000.00 this year the sum is not less, and this rule does not set it.
